title: Best Time to Visit Motovun, Croatia: Seasonal Guide 2027
metaDescription: When to visit Motovun in 2027: September–October is the best balance of weather, crowds and price. See how each season compares, plus festival and truffle tips.
content:
## When Is the Best Time to Visit Motovun?

September to early October gives the best balance of weather, crowds and price. Days are comfortable for walking the ramparts, restaurants and konobas are open, and the surrounding Motovun Forest is in white truffle season. May and June come second. They are greener and cheaper than July, and the town is not yet crowded.

Motovun is a small hilltop town in inland Istria, not a beach destination. The old core can be seen in about two hours, so timing matters less for sights than for atmosphere, food and whether places are open. That is why the season you choose changes the trip more than it would in a coastal resort.

## Season-by-Season Verdict

### Autumn (September–October): The Best Overall Choice

Autumn is the main reason to come. Truffle season runs roughly from September to December, and the area around Motovun, Livade and Buzet is the centre of Croatian truffle production. Vineyards are in harvest, temperatures are around 20–25°C, and the valley turns red and gold.

Autumn also has a packed event calendar. In 2026 the Motovun Festival of Teran Wine and Truffles ran on 17–18 October, Tuber Fest in Livade on 24–25 October, and Zigante Truffle Days in Livade on weekends from early October to 1 November. Dates move slightly each year, so check them before booking 2027.

The trade-offs are higher prices for white truffle dishes and a busier town on festival weekends. Book guided truffle hunts ahead, because availability depends on weather, group size and guide schedules.

### Spring (Late April–June): Best Value

Spring suits walkers and cyclists. The Mirna Valley is green, wild asparagus appears on menus, and the town is quiet. Accommodation is typically cheaper than in July and August, and you avoid the heat of midday on the exposed ramparts. Black truffles are available all year, so a truffle meal is still possible, though it is not the headline attraction it is in autumn.

### Summer (July–August): Only for a Reason

Summer has the longest days and the warmest weather, and every restaurant and shop is open. It is also the most expensive and most crowded period. The exception is the Motovun Film Festival, held in late July and lasting about five days, with open-air screenings in the main square.

The festival is the one summer reason worth the premium. Book accommodation months ahead, because Motovun has few beds and prices rise sharply. For a general visit, skip peak July and August and use the savings elsewhere.

### Winter (November–March): Quiet, With Caveats

November and early December still fall within truffle season, which makes them a sensible budget alternative to October. From January to March the town is very quiet, often foggy, and some restaurants and shops close or shorten their hours. Daytime temperatures are around 5–10°C. Parking is cheapest in this period at about €2.

## Quick Comparison: Weather, Crowds and Price

| Priority | Best window |
|---|---|
| Food and truffles | Late September to October |
| Lowest crowds with good weather | May to mid-June |
| Cheapest with most venues open | November to early December |
| Film and nightlife | Late July (festival) |
| Photography and fog | November to February |

## Opinion: Skip the Film Festival Unless You Love Film

Motovun's summer reputation rests on the film festival, but it is the weakest choice for most visitors. Rooms are scarce and expensive, the town is at its busiest, and the quiet hilltop atmosphere is gone. A weekday in late September or a weekend in mid-May gives you a better version of Motovun for less money.

## Insider Tips for Timing a Visit

- **Stay one night.** The town is at its best in early morning and evening, after day-trippers have left.
- **Book truffle hunts early** for October weekends, when demand is highest.
- **Use weekdays in autumn.** Festival events cluster on Saturdays and Sundays, so midweek visits are calmer.
- **Bring a car.** Public transport inland is limited, and a car makes nearby villages, wine cellars and truffle areas much easier to reach.
- **Plan for the parking system.** Cars cannot be driven into the old core, so allow time for the walk up from the parking areas below the walls.
- **Wear comfortable shoes.** The cobbled lanes and rampart walk are steep in places.

## Who Should Go When

- **Food and wine travellers:** late September to October.
- **Hikers and cyclists:** May to June, and September.
- **Budget travellers:** May, early June, or November.
- **Film fans:** late July, with a booking made well in advance.
- **Combining with a beach holiday:** June or September, when you can add coastal Istria without peak-season prices.

faq.question: What is the best month to visit Motovun?
faq.answer: October is the best single month for food lovers, thanks to white truffle season, wine harvest and several truffle festivals. For quieter streets and cheaper rooms, choose May or early June. September works well for both.

faq.question: When is truffle season in Motovun?
faq.answer: White truffle season runs from about September to December, with the busiest events in October. Black truffles can be found all year, and they are cheaper than white ones. Guided hunts should be booked ahead in autumn.

faq.question: When is the Motovun Film Festival?
faq.answer: It takes place in late July and lasts about five days. Screenings are held in the main square and other venues. Book accommodation and tickets early, because the town is small and fills quickly.

faq.question: Is Motovun worth visiting in winter?
faq.answer: Yes, if you want quiet streets, fog and low prices, and you accept the limits. Some restaurants and shops close or open for fewer hours from January to March. November and early December are better because truffle season is still running.

faq.question: Is Motovun too crowded in summer?
faq.answer: July and August are the busiest months, and late July is the peak because of the film festival. The town is small, so day-trippers and festival crowds are noticeable. Staying overnight and walking the ramparts early or late helps.

faq.question: How long should you spend in Motovun?
faq.answer: Half a day covers the old town and ramparts. A full day allows time for a truffle hunt or a wine tasting nearby. One overnight stay is the best way to see the town after the day-trippers have left.

quickAnswer: The best time to visit Motovun is September to early October, with a good second choice in May to June. Both periods have mild weather, open restaurants, manageable crowds and the truffle and wine harvest in autumn. Late July suits film fans only, and winter is quiet and has limited hours.
